newsitem.title: USA: NextLevel wins $240 mln wireless contracts.
newsitem.headline: NextLevel wins $240 mln wireless contracts.

text.p: General Instrument Corp said on Monday that its NextLevel Broadband Networks Group was selected to provide digital wireless systems to People's Choice TV Corp and CS Wireless Systems Inc.

PCTV and CS Wireless, which have a combined total of 15.1 million line of sight homes, have committed to ordering 600,000 DWT-1000 digital wireless consumer set-tops and headend equipment over three years.
The total value of the award is about $240 million, according to NextLevel.

"Our NextLevel digital wireless system and consumer terminals will enable operators to significantly increase their channel capacity and provide state-of-the-art digital video, audio and interactive data services," said Glenn Altchek, a NextLevel manager.

It said the set-tops offer subscribers sharper video images, CD-quality sound, more channels and interactive services that include near-video-on-demand, virtual channel services and high-speed Internet access. They also support electronic program guides and broadcast interactive services.

People's Choice owns and operates wireless cable television systems in Chicago, Detroit, Houston, Phoenix, St. Louis and Tucson, and holds wireless cable frequency rights in Indianapolis, Kansas City and Milwaukee.

CS Wireless is a privately held company formed by a partnership of Heartland Wireless Communications Inc, CAI Wireless Systems Inc, Bell Atlantic Corp, and NYNEX Corp. It operates wireless cable systems that serve about 70,000 customers in nine U.S. markets.
